title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 10
statement: A triangle with side lengths in the ratio \(3:4:5\) is inscribed in a circle of radius \(3.\) What is the area of the triangle?

solutions.text:
Let the sides be \(3x,\) \(4x,\) and \(5x.\) The triangle is right, so its hypotenuse is a diameter.

Thus \(5x=2\cdot 3=6,\) giving \(x=\tfrac65.\)

The area is \(\tfrac12\cdot 3x\cdot 4x=6x^2\) \(=6\cdot\tfrac{36}{25}\) \(=\tfrac{216}{25}=8.64.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: A \(3\!:\!4\!:\!5\) triangle is right-angled, so its hypotenuse is a diameter of the circle
The hypotenuse \(5x\) equals the diameter \(6,\) then the area is \(\tfrac12(3x)(4x)\)
